The master-slave dialectic exemplifies this dynamic, demonstrating how domination paradoxically produces dependency and how genuine freedom requires mutual acknowledgment rather than unilateral control. Subsequent interpreters, from Marx to Sartre, have appropriated and transformed these insights to articulate theories of alienation, authenticity, and collective liberation, each emphasizing different dimensions of Hegel's systematic project.
